reconcile.connective: Commentators harmonize by sequence and emphasis: Caleb spoke first and most forcefully in 13:30, while Joshua stood with him and joined the open appeal in 14:6.

discrepancy.connective: Steven DiMattei argues the two scenes are a source-critical doublet — the Yahwist's Judah-centered version features Caleb alone, while the Priestly version adds Joshua of Ephraim for a unified Israel, so the single-vs-double speaker is a seam, not a sequence.

skeptic.name: Steven DiMattei
skeptic.work: Contradictions in the Bible, #238 ("In the face of there being giants in the land, who encourages the people to have faith in Yahweh: Caleb alone OR Caleb and Joshua?")
skeptic.attribution: Steven DiMattei, Contradictions in the Bible #238 (contradictionsinthebible.com, 2013)

excerpts.excerpt_text: The fact that Caleb only is mentioned, though, according to Num 14:6, Joshua also stood by his side, may be explained on the simple ground, that at first Caleb was the only one to speak and maintain the possibility of conquering Canaan.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Names both 13:30 and 14:6 and harmonizes the single-vs-double speaker directly: Caleb spoke first; Joshua stood with him. The strongest single reconcile on the row.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Caleb encouraged them to go forward, though he was seconded by Joshua only (Num 13:30) …
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Reads 13:30 as Caleb speaking while Joshua seconds him — the same first-speaker harmonization in a distinct voice. Trimmed at the colon, so ends with the elision marker.

excerpts.excerpt_text: Caleb and Joshua (see 14:6, 10, 30) were more optimistic in their assessment of the land than the other spies were (cp. 14:31-33).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Glosses the 13:30 actor as Caleb and Joshua jointly, cross-referencing 14:6 — treats the two scenes as one stance, dissolving the single-speaker reading.

pd_work.resource: Keil & Delitzsch, Biblical Commentary on the Old Testament (1861-75), on Numbers 13:30
pd_work.author: Keil & Delitzsch
pd_work.note: Treats this exact pair: Caleb alone in 13:30 is harmonized with Joshua at his side in 14:6 on the ground that Caleb was the first to speak.
